seo.title: Challenges · Ontario Rare Action Group
seo.description: From the moment a symptom appears to decades into living with a rare condition, Ontario families navigate a healthcare system that wasn't built for them.

header.title: The challenges nobody warns you about.
header.lede: From the moment a symptom appears to decades into living with a rare condition, Ontario families navigate a healthcare system that wasn't built for them. Here's what we hear, every day.

challenges.title: The diagnostic odyssey
challenges.desc: Most patients see seven or more specialists before receiving an accurate diagnosis. That delay costs jobs, marriages, savings — and in some cases, lives.

challenges.title: No treatment, no roadmap
challenges.desc: Even with a diagnosis in hand, the majority of rare-disease patients have no approved therapy and no specialist clinic to manage their condition long-term.

challenges.title: Unaffordable and unfunded
challenges.desc: Where therapies do exist, costs can exceed $250,000 per year — and provincial coverage decisions can take half a decade to land.

challenges.title: Geographic inequity
challenges.desc: Patients in rural and northern Ontario travel hours — sometimes days — to reach a specialist who has even heard of their condition.

challenges.title: Caregivers carry it alone
challenges.desc: Family caregivers provide the equivalent of a full-time job in unpaid labour, with little recognition in provincial policy or labour law.

challenges.title: Mental health falls through the cracks
challenges.desc: Rare-disease patients and their caregivers report rates of anxiety and depression more than double the general population — yet specialized supports are scarce.

challenges.title: A research gap that compounds
challenges.desc: Fewer than 5% of rare diseases attract a single dedicated research grant in Canada, leaving most conditions invisible to the systems meant to study them.

quote.text: Rare doesn't mean a small problem — it means seven thousand small problems the system has chosen not to solve at scale.
quote.attribution: Dr. Sofia Reyes · Pediatric geneticist · Hamilton Health Sciences

ctaBand.heading: These challenges are solvable.
ctaBand.body: Each one of them maps to a concrete commitment in our advocacy platform. See what we're doing about it — and add your name.
